# SPD-047 — Bash hook: a git alias in a config file the hook cannot read (-C or --git-dir repo config, HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME, ~/.gitconfig) runs a write verb

## Brief
SPD-044 refuses -c/--config-env and environment config injection, but git also reads aliases from config files the hook does not open: another repository's .git/config reached with 'git -C <repo>' or '--git-dir <dir>', the user's ~/.gitconfig, and the global config git finds through HOME ($HOME/.gitconfig) or XDG_CONFIG_HOME ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config) when either is set on the line (Spud added these two at creation; SPD-044 does not read them). A member who can write such a file could define 'alias.p = push' there and then run 'git -C <repo> p' or 'HOME=<dir> git p'. None are configured today (git config --get-regexp alias. is empty), so this is latent, but the hook has no way to read an on-disk alias table.

Evidence: git honours [alias] in any config file it loads; probed at SPD-044 that a GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL file with [alias] v=version makes 'git v' run version. The -C, --git-dir, HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME cases were not probed. Writing another repo's .git/config or ~/.gitconfig is normally outside a member's deliverables (the edit hook refuses it), which limits reach, but a shell redirection into a directory outside the repository may not be. Out of SPD-044's brief, which named it a proposal candidate.
